editorialNote: Focused KB for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The DMD pipeline is dominated by exon-skipping antisense oligonucleotides (eteplirsen exon 51, golodirsen/viltolarsen exon 53, casimersen exon 45), corticosteroid regimens (prednisone, deflazacort, vamorolone), HDAC inhibition (givinostat Duvyzat approved 2024), and AAV microdystrophin gene therapy (delandistrogene moxeparvovec / Elevidys, approved 2023 with expanded indication 2024 that generated safety concerns). Any DMD output that fails to mention Elevidys or Duvyzat is AI slop. Pfizer's fordadistrogene movaparvovec (PF-06939926) was discontinued in 2024 following the CIFFREO phase 3 failure.

commonComorbidities: Dilated cardiomyopathy (primary cause of death in modern era)
Learning / behavioral difficulties (~30%, dystrophin isoform in brain)
lifestyleCategories: Multidisciplinary Certified Duchenne Care Center enrollment (PPMD network)
Cardiac surveillance (echo/MRI yearly from diagnosis; initiate ACEi/ARB by age 10 or per guideline even if asymptomatic)
Pulmonary function testing yearly after LoA; non-invasive ventilation when indicated
Bone health monitoring (DXA yearly on steroids; vitamin D + calcium; bisphosphonate for vertebral fractures)
Orthotic management (AFOs; KAFOs for prolonged ambulation assistance)
School-based special education support (IEP) for learning/behavioral issues
Genetic counseling for carrier mothers/sisters (DMD is X-linked)

items.title: Diagnosis and management of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, part 1: diagnosis, and neuromuscular, rehabilitation, endocrine, and gastrointestinal and nutritional management
items.authors: Birnkrant DJ, Bushby K, Bann CM, et al.
items.summary: Modern international DMD Care Considerations, part 1 of 3. Covers diagnosis, neuromuscular management (including corticosteroid initiation), rehabilitation, endocrine, GI, and nutrition. Standard reference for every non-genetic aspect of DMD management.

items.title: Diagnosis and management of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, part 2: respiratory, cardiac, bone health, and orthopaedic management
items.authors: Birnkrant DJ, Bushby K, Bann CM, et al.
items.summary: DMD Care Considerations, part 2 — respiratory (PFT frequency, NIV, cough assist), cardiac (yearly echo/MRI, early ACEi/ARB), bone (DXA, bisphosphonate for vertebral fractures), orthopaedic (scoliosis surgery).

items.title: ELEVIDYS (delandistrogene moxeparvovec-rokl) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: First AAV-based gene therapy for DMD. Delivers Elevidys micro-dystrophin transgene. Accelerated approval June 2023 for ambulatory patients 4-5 years; label EXPANDED June 2024 to all ambulatory patients ≥4 years (traditional approval) and non-ambulatory patients ≥4 years (accelerated approval) despite primary endpoint miss in EMBARK. Two deaths in non-ambulatory patients post-expansion triggered safety review. Boxed/warning concerns include acute liver injury, immune-mediated myositis, myocarditis.

keyPassages.quote: ELEVIDYS is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in ambulatory and non-ambulatory pediatric patients aged 4 years and older with a confirmed mutation in the DMD gene.
Acute serious liver injury, immune-mediated myositis, myocarditis, and acute respiratory failure have been reported with ELEVIDYS.

items.title: DUVYZAT (givinostat) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: First FDA-approved non-steroid disease-modifying DMD therapy (March 2024). Oral HDAC inhibitor given twice daily. Approved for ambulatory patients ≥6 years with confirmed DMD mutation. EPIDYS phase 3 showed slowing of 4-stair climb decline. Key monitoring: platelet count (thrombocytopenia), triglycerides, QT interval.

keyPassages.quote: DUVYZAT is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 6 years of age and older.

items.title: AGAMREE (vamorolone) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: Dissociative steroid that retains efficacy of prednisone/deflazacort on motor outcomes but with reduced growth suppression and bone-mineral-density loss. FDA-approved October 2023 for DMD in patients ≥2 years. VISION-DMD pivotal trial basis. Alternative to prednisone/deflazacort where growth/bone side effects are intolerable.

keyPassages.quote: AGAMREE is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy in patients 2 years of age and older.

items.title: Pfizer discontinues DMD gene therapy PF-06939926 (fordadistrogene movaparvovec) following CIFFREO phase 3 failure
items.summary: June 2024 — Pfizer announced discontinuation of development for fordadistrogene movaparvovec (PF-06939926, an AAV9-based DMD microdystrophin gene therapy) after the CIFFREO phase 3 failed to meet its primary endpoint. This leaves Elevidys as the only marketed AAV DMD gene therapy. Patients and families following Pfizer's program must be informed it is not moving forward.

keyPassages.quote: Pfizer today announced the discontinuation of development of its investigational gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD).

canonicalFacts.claim: Elevidys (delandistrogene moxeparvovec, Sarepta) is the only FDA-approved AAV gene therapy for DMD; label expanded June 2024 to ambulatory and non-ambulatory patients ≥4 years despite EMBARK primary endpoint miss.
Duvyzat (givinostat, Italfarmaco) is the first non-steroid oral disease-modifying DMD therapy (FDA March 2024).
Agamree (vamorolone) is a dissociative steroid approved October 2023 as an alternative to prednisone/deflazacort with less growth and bone impact.
Exon-skipping antisense oligonucleotides: eteplirsen (exon 51), golodirsen (exon 53), viltolarsen (exon 53), casimersen (exon 45) — all accelerated approvals with controversial efficacy evidence.
Pfizer discontinued its DMD AAV gene therapy PF-06939926 in June 2024 after the CIFFREO phase 3 trial failed.

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Start corticosteroid therapy (prednisone, deflazacort, or vamorolone) at ~age 4-6 years per current consensus; vamorolone when growth/bone side effects of prednisone/deflazacort are prohibitive.
Cardiac surveillance: echo/MRI yearly; initiate ACE inhibitor or ARB by age 10 (or earlier per cardiologist) regardless of symptoms.
Pulmonary function testing yearly after loss of ambulation; non-invasive ventilation when indicated.
Bone health: vitamin D, calcium, yearly DXA on steroids; bisphosphonate for vertebral compression fractures.
Physical therapy with stretching; avoid eccentric (resistive) exercise that may worsen muscle damage.
Genetic counseling for mothers (carrier testing + cardiac evaluation) and sisters.

redFlags: Physicians generally caution against administering Elevidys without AAVrh74 antibody screening + LFT baseline + close post-infusion monitoring for acute liver injury, myocarditis, and immune-mediated myositis.
Physicians generally caution against skipping cardiac surveillance even in ambulatory boys — DMD cardiomyopathy can progress silently until late.
Literature warns against metformin for 'DMD exercise mimetic' — no approved DMD indication; RCT evidence insufficient.
Physicians generally caution against prescribing statins or fibrates to DMD patients on long-term corticosteroids without specialist input.
Offshore stem-cell or 'gene therapy' clinics (China, Mexico, Panama) offering unapproved AAV or cell infusions for DMD — patient-safety concern, no peer-reviewed efficacy data, FDA warning letters.
Physicians generally caution against withholding genetic testing — the specific DMD mutation determines eligibility for ALL DMD-specific therapies.

pipelineDrugs.name: Delandistrogene moxeparvovec
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA accelerated approval June 2023 (ages 4-5); label EXPANDED June 2024 to all ambulatory and non-ambulatory ≥4 years. Two deaths in non-ambulatory patients in 2024-2025 triggered safety review.
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Only FDA-approved AAV gene therapy for DMD. Safety signal in non-ambulatory expansion is important context for any recommendation.

pipelineDrugs.name: Givinostat
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA approval March 2024 for DMD ≥6 years (EPIDYS phase 3)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First non-steroid oral disease-modifying DMD therapy. Works regardless of specific DMD mutation.

pipelineDrugs.name: Vamorolone
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Dissociative steroid; retains NF-κB inhibition while reducing gene-regulation side effects
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA approval October 2023 for DMD ≥2 years
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Alternative to prednisone/deflazacort with less growth suppression and bone loss.

pipelineDrugs.name: Prednisone
pipelineDrugs.status: Standard of care (typically 0.75 mg/kg/day) per care considerations
pipelineDrugs.approvalStatus: approved (off-label for DMD historically; now guideline-endorsed)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Historic DMD backbone; still widely used. Duvyzat and Elevidys supplement, do not replace, corticosteroid therapy.

pipelineDrugs.name: Deflazacort
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Alternative to prednisone with slightly different side-effect profile (less weight gain, similar bone loss).

pipelineDrugs.name: Eteplirsen
pipelineDrugs.status: Accelerated FDA approval 2016 for exon-51-amenable DMD
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First DMD-specific mutation-targeted therapy. Controversial approval based on surrogate dystrophin expression.

pipelineDrugs.name: Viltolarsen
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Second exon-53 ASO; same amenability as golodirsen.

pipelineDrugs.name: Ataluren
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Readthrough of premature stop codons (for nonsense mutations)
pipelineDrugs.status: EMA conditional approval (EU) 2014; NOT FDA-approved (advisory committee voted against; FDA denied 2017 and again 2023). EMA CHMP recommended NON-RENEWAL January 2024; conversion/withdrawal pending.
pipelineDrugs.approvalStatus: approved (EU, but non-renewal recommended 2024); not approved (US)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: EU-only access; EMA committee recommended non-renewal in 2024. Patients and families in the US may ask about it; needs accurate framing.

pipelineDrugs.name: Fordadistrogene movaparvovec
pipelineDrugs.status: DISCONTINUED June 2024 after CIFFREO phase 3 failure
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Pfizer's major DMD program; ended 2024. Must be addressed as discontinued for families following the field.

pipelineDrugs.name: Solid Biosciences SGT-003
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Next-generation AAV microdystrophin with differential capsid
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Competitor to Elevidys; early clinical stage; follows earlier SGT-001 program that was paused for safety.

pipelineDrugs.name: RGX-202
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Third AAV microdystrophin in active clinical development.

excludedAgents.name: Fordadistrogene movaparvovec (Pfizer PF-06939926)
excludedAgents.reason: Phase 3 CIFFREO failed in 2024; Pfizer discontinued the program June 2024.

excludedAgents.name: Offshore stem-cell clinics offering IV MSC or 'gene therapy' for DMD
excludedAgents.reason: No peer-reviewed efficacy data for DMD. FDA warning letters to US-linked operators. Patient-safety concern.

excludedAgents.name: Metformin + L-citrulline (unproven 'exercise mimetic' combination)
excludedAgents.reason: Small open-label studies; no rigorous RCT support; not a guideline-endorsed therapy.

excludedAgents.name: Coenzyme Q10 for DMD
excludedAgents.reason: No RCT evidence of benefit on motor outcomes.

excludedAgents.name: Creatine monohydrate as primary therapy for DMD
excludedAgents.reason: Some small studies suggest short-term strength modest effects; NOT a disease-modifying therapy. Should not substitute for corticosteroid, exon-skipping, or gene therapy discussion.
